summary: Under TXR150000, land disturbance determines the construction stormwater track when runoff reaches or is adjacent to state surface water. The common plan counts; small sites are 1 to less than 5 acres; large sites are 5 acres or more.
evidence: regulated according to the area of land disturbed
trigger: Disturbance ≥1 acre including larger common plan, with covered runoff.

summary: In its October 19, 2026 response TCEQ reported pausing permit issuance for construction or development of infrastructure directly supporting data centers, screening pending applications and some claimed authorizations. This is an agency action reported on that date; confirm present implementation with TCEQ. It does not establish a local zoning ban.
locator: October 19 response, p. 1; screening of permits and claimed authorizations
evidence: directly supporting data centers

summary: City staff’s account of adopted UDO 2026-4719 identifies a data center use and a 5,000-square-foot size criterion in its definition. Council may condition a conditional use permit for compatibility, including noise, lighting and buffering. Check the district table for a parcel.
locator: UDO amendment (data center definition); compare UDO §§6.3.C, 11.2
evidence: accessory structure larger than 5,000 square feet

summary: An owner whose aggregate withdrawal capacity exceeds 100,000 gallons in one day across all methods and ground/surface sources must register within three months after completion and report use annually. This is capacity-based registration, not a zoning or withdrawal permit.
locator: Significant Water Withdrawal Facility Registration; IC 14-25-7-15
evidence: in the aggregate from all sources and by all methods

summary: In unincorporated Lake County, Ordinance 2590 places data centers in the special-exception category in M-1 and M-2. The industrial zone alone does not confer a right to build. §154-8-090 supplies additional application requirements; consult subsequent amendments for submittal details.
evidence: SPECIAL EXCEPTION USE IN THE M-1
district: M-1 light industrial; M-2 heavy industrial

summary: A special-exception applicant must provide written verification from Northern Indiana Public Services Company (NIPSCO) on capacity for the facility and current/future area needs, adequate equipment sizing and absence of interference or line-voltage fluctuations.
evidence: Adequate capacity is available in the supply lines and substation

summary: For qualifying construction stormwater discharges entering state surface waters or a connected storm drain, Ohio EPA permits cover disturbance of at least one acre, including smaller sites in a common plan ultimately meeting the threshold. Individual or watershed-specific requirements can apply.
locator: Ohio EPA Permit OHC000006, Part I.B.1, printed p. 3
evidence: The threshold acreage includes the entire area disturbed

summary: With the exceptions in divisions (D) and (E), new or increased consumptive use of state waters above an average of two million gallons/day in any 30-day period requires a Division of Water Resources permit. Gross withdrawal and purchased utility water are not interchangeable with this trigger.
evidence: more than an average of two million gallons of water per day
trigger: New/increased consumptive use >2,000,000 US gal/day, 30-day average

summary: The city identifies data centers as permitted under the GE and TMD base texts, with overlays/site-specific zoning affecting eligibility. It says rezoning applications approved beginning April 2025 excluded data centers as a primary use. Check the adopted site text before classifying a parcel.
locator: FAQ → What kind of zoning code has New Albany adopted?; annexation/zoning discussion
evidence: all approved rezoning applications have excluded data centers as a primary use

summary: Trustees report adopting a 12-month data center zoning moratorium on July 13, 2026. This is township zoning in Clermont County, not a statewide measure.
evidence: passed a Zoning Moratorium on Data Centers in Ohio Township
trigger: Twelve months; check for amendment or termination.

summary: Where ADEQ administers AZPDES, its construction general permit covers construction stormwater entering Arizona surface waters directly or through an MS4 leading to those waters. Count the larger common plan in the one-acre disturbance threshold.
locator: AZG2025-001, Part 1: obtaining coverage and eligibility
evidence: part of a larger common plan of development or sale
trigger: ≥1 acre including common plan plus qualifying discharge

summary: Under Chapter 35 §2214, Chandler limits primary-use data centers to PAD zoning; ancillary facilities are subject to distinct location, purpose and size restrictions. PAD designation alone is not project approval.
evidence: primary use only permitted in planning area development

summary: The city requires a pre-construction baseline sound study, mitigation relative to that baseline and annual noise studies at peak operation for five years after construction.
evidence: annual noise study during peak operation times for five years

summary: Except as specified in NRS 533.325, an applicant must apply to the State Engineer before work to appropriate public water or change the diversion, use type or use location of an existing appropriation. Utility purchases alone are not a new direct appropriation.
evidence: apply to the State Engineer for a permit
trigger: Appropriation or change; exceptions include NRS 533.027, 533.028 and 534.065.

summary: Reno says new data centers require a conditional use permit. Check the separate moratorium before treating this as an available application route.
locator: Data Center Text Amendment and Moratorium
evidence: require approval of a conditional use permit

summary: The city reports its June 1, 2026 resolution suspends acceptance of data center conditional use permit applications through August 31, 2027, or until adequate regulations are adopted.
evidence: through August 31, 2027, or until a time that adequate regulations are adopted
trigger: New data center conditional use permit application

summary: MDEQ screens direct groundwater or surface-water withdrawals based on source and method. A permit may be necessary; do not characterize all data centers buying municipal water as direct permit applicants.
locator: Environmental Permitting in Mississippi → Water Use
evidence: Depending on the source and method of withdrawal

summary: Stationary emissions equipment, including emergency generators or other onsite generation, may require air permitting. MDEQ distinguishes this review from zoning, noise and utility rates.
locator: Environmental Permitting in Mississippi → Air Permitting
evidence: including emergency generators or other onsite power-generation equipment

authority: City of Ridgeland Mayor and Board of Aldermen
summary: Ordinance 2023-09 added data centers and related facilities to the Technical Industrial Park permitted-use list. This is use permission, not an exemption from site or building review.
evidence: Data Center including Data Center Related Facilities

summary: For commercial applicants, architectural review and approval by the mayor and aldermen precedes the city's review of construction plans. Verify whether this process applies to the proposed development classification.
evidence: commercial applicants must obtain approval by the Mayor and Board of Aldermen

authority: Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation
summary: TDEC directs an applicant proposing to withdraw at least 10,000 gallons per day from a surface-water or groundwater source to register with the Division of Water Resources. Registration itself neither authorizes nor limits the withdrawal. Do not apply the threshold directly to water bought from a city.
locator: TDEC Data Centers → Water Withdrawal Registration
evidence: 10,000 or more gallons per day from surface or groundwater sources
trigger: Proposed direct withdrawal ≥10,000 US gallons/day; check statutory exceptions.

authority: Metropolitan Council of Nashville and Davidson County
summary: The adopted use table classifies large data centers as an industrial use requiring special exception in IR and IG and disallows the separately defined campus category in any district. Apply the ordinance definitions before using the table, and check the temporary permit pause.
evidence: industrial use permitted by special exception
district: IR and IG (large); no permitted district (campus)

authority: Metropolitan Council of Nashville and Davidson County
summary: Zoning applicants must provide written confirmation that the water and sewer utility has reviewed capacity to serve the project; insufficient utility capacity prevents zoning permit approval.
evidence: insufficient water and/or sewer capacity to service the data center

summary: For the statutory industrial-area subpart, construction and operation of data centers and directly related commercial activities count as industrial purposes. This definition does not grant statewide by-right zoning or replace parish zoning.
evidence: construction and operation of data centers and commercial operations directly related thereto

summary: Parish Ordinance 26-6-3 lists data centers as permitted uses in M-1 and M-2 subject to supplemental use and performance rules. Treat the parish as a county-equivalent when joining geography, not as a city.
locator: Ordinance 26-6-3, Appendix A §VI.D and §VII; final action June 1, 2026
evidence: Data Centers as permitted uses in the M-1 and M-2 zoning districts

authority: New Mexico Environment Department Air Quality Bureau
summary: Where NMED has air jurisdiction, a new or modified emitting facility must screen its potential emissions before construction. For example, above 10 lb/hour of a criteria pollutant other than VOCs triggers the Part 72 construction-permit screen; separate annual, toxic and major-source thresholds also apply. Check the authority for Bernalillo County and tribal lands.
locator: Types of Permits → Minor Source Construction Permit (Part 72)
evidence: More than 10 pounds per hour of criteria pollutants
trigger: Potential emissions; >10 lb/h is one screening route, not the sole test.

authority: Santa Fe County Board of County Commissioners
summary: The recorded ordinance pauses county development approvals and permits for covered facilities/expansions with proposed aggregate IT load of at least 1 MW for 18 months from recording, subject to extension. Incidental equipment, qualifying county governmental facilities, complete prior applications and vested rights are addressed separately.
evidence: has a proposed aggregate IT Load Capacity of 1 megawatt(s) or greater
trigger: Proposed aggregate IT load ≥1 MW; exceptions in §§2, 4, 6.

authority: Metropolitan Council of Nashville and Davidson County
summary: The council’s amended temporary moratorium pauses acceptance, processing, approval and issuance of data center zoning, building or grading permits or administrative appeals until December 1, 2026. Consult subsequent council action at the end of that period.
locator: BL2026-1448 as amended, Amendment No. 1 §1; see July 2026 council action and DCB Nashville case, October 6 order
evidence: until December 1, 2026
trigger: Covered data center development in Nashville and Davidson County; temporal overlay.

summary: Subject to the statutory exceptions, withdrawal from a nonexempt well within an active management area requires a groundwater withdrawal permit. A general industrial use permit is one listed category. Check the water source, service area, exemption and separate qualifying criteria before applying this to a data center.
evidence: groundwater from a nonexempt well in an active management area
trigger: Nonexempt well + active management area; statutory exceptions apply.
